- **Moratorium ID:** `ny-manlius-2026`

### Town of Brookhaven

- **Type:** Town

- **Outcome:** Town Board unanimously approved an 18-month moratorium on all new data-center applications following a five-hour hearing with about 300 attendees and 60 speakers opposed

### Town of Dryden (Tompkins County)

- **Type:** Town
- **Status:** ⚪ Replaced
- **Date enacted:** 2024-07-31
- **Normalized date:** `2024-07-31` (exact)
- **Duration:** 18 months as initially adopted; extension draft (Local Law No. 1 of 2026) would change term to 20 months [VERIFY: signed, filed Local Law No. 1 of 2026 not in captured Dryden Local Laws index as of 2026-04-29; permanent zoning Local Law No. 2 of 2026 was instead adopted 2026-02-19]
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `ny-dryden-2024`
- **Legal basis:** Local Law No. 2 of 2024; draft Local Law No. 1 of 2026 extension; Local Law No. 2 of 2026 replacement zoning definitions
- **What prompted it:** Proposed commercial cryptocurrency/data-processing use in Freeville area, regulatory gap, and stated concern for natural, historic, cultural, and electrical resources
- **Affected projects:** New York Metro Cloud LLC proposed use (cryptocurrency hosting/mining) at 2186 Dryden Road in Freeville. No MW/power-capacity figure appears in any available record; federal court filings (Bartolini v. Town of Dryden, N.D.N.Y. lead case 3:24-cv-01380, member 3:24-cv-01383, plus related S.D.N.Y. dockets 7:24-cv-07062 and 7:24-cv-05925) describe the site as a 0.24-acre parcel with approximately 3,000 square feet of interior space in a converted Quonset-style building -- consistent with a small hosting operation rather than a utility-scale, megawatt-rated data center, which explains why no MW figure exists rather than it simply being unreported.
- **Detailed status:** Replaced by permanent zoning action adopted 2026-02-19; moratorium term otherwise would have expired in early 2026
- **Outcome:** Town adopted a 2026 zoning law defining data centers, accessory data centers, cryptocurrency, and cryptocurrency data mines, while taking no action to add data centers or cryptocurrency facilities to the allowable-use chart. This appears to prohibit principal data center and cryptocurrency data mine uses unless later code amendments allow them.

### Town of Lansing (Tompkins County) - proposed, not enacted

- **Type:** Town
- **Status:** 🔴 Rescinded
- **Date enacted:** Not enacted. Public hearing held 2025-09-24; the Town Board's resolution withdrawing the proposed moratorium (Local Law #7 of 2025) is confirmed on the November 19, 2025 Town Board meeting agenda (Item 4, Motions and Resolutions: "Resolution Withdrawing Proposed Moratorium (Local Law #7 of 2025)").
- **Normalized date:** `—` (unverified)
- **Duration:** Proposed 365 days
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ny-lansing-2025`
- **Legal basis:** Proposed Local Law No. 7 of 2025; resolution withdrawing proposed moratorium
- **What prompted it:** Town zoning rewrite and EPOD planning process, plus local concern about large commercial and industrial projects including the TeraWulf Cayuga Data Campus
- **Affected projects:** TeraWulf/Cayuga Operating Company proposed Cayuga Data Campus at the former Cayuga coal plant; TeraWulf press release describes rights to develop up to 400 MW and 138 MW expected ready for service in 2026
- **Detailed status:** Withdrawn before enactment
- **Outcome:** Moratorium proposal withdrawn November 19, 2025. The Lansing Zoning Board of Appeals ruled on December 23, 2025 that the proposed AI/HPC data center is a permitted "general processing" use under existing industrial/research zoning; Cayuga Lake Action Now (CLEAN) and FLX Strong filed an Article 78 petition in NY State Supreme Court on January 30, 2026 against the Lansing ZBA and TeraWulf challenging that ruling. The outcome of the Article 78 petition was not confirmed as of this pass (2026-07-31); the last located update was an April 14, 2026 report on a separate state water-permit approval for the associated power plant, which could not be accessed this pass due to source rate-limiting.

### Town of Lewiston (Niagara County) - proposed, public hearing held

- **Type:** Town
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** Adopted as Local Law No. 3 of 2026, now filed in the Town's official 2026 Local Laws register; the exact Town Board vote date was not confirmed from a source I could directly read, but adoption followed the 2026-04-13 public hearing.
- **Normalized date:** `—` (unverified)
- **Duration:** Eighteen (18) months from the effective date of adoption (the 'Moratorium Period'), extendable by Town Board resolution for additional periods not to exceed six months each.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `ny-lewiston-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Proposed Local Law 3-2026
- **What prompted it:** General/preemptive moratorium. The enacted law's legislative findings (Section 3) cite electrical and wastewater infrastructure capacity, fire safety, the absence of a zoning framework for these uses in the Town Code, and a pending Comprehensive Plan update -- no specific project or applicant is named anywhere in the enacted text.
- **Affected projects:** None. The adopted law is townwide and general; no applicant or project is named in its findings or operative sections.
- **Detailed status:** Adopted and in effect as Local Law No. 3 of 2026, an 18-month moratorium on the establishment, construction, expansion, or operation of data centers (aggregate IT load >= 1 MW), artificial intelligence processing facilities (>= 1 MW), and cryptocurrency mining operations (aggregate electrical draw >= 100 kW), with a SEQRA Type II Action determination under 6 NYCRR 617.5(c)(33).
- **Outcome:** Pending. Captured agenda describes a local law imposing a moratorium on establishment, construction, expansion, or operation of covered facilities.
